mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) following two consecutive quarterly declines in GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which compresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) following four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and rapid decline in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 1% for two months signals a deflationary monetary policy stance, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls and CPIAUCSL < 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both FEDFUNDS falls and CPIAUCSL < 1% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) over three months signals robust household demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both rise for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when both PAYEMS and HOUST rise for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressure and boosts consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) following six consecutive months of PAYEMS above its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive GDP growth signal (GDPC1 rising above 3% q/q annualized for two consecutive quarters) in a non-inflationary environment (CPIAUCSL stable, < 2% y/y) indicates sustainable demand expansion, which supports earnings growth and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 3% q/q annualized for two consecutive quarters and CPIAUCSL < 2% y/y
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when GDPC1 exceeds 3% q/q annualized for two quarters and CPIAUCSL remains below 2% y/y.
